q: Where do I find the Voice Isolation effect?
a: Effects panel ▸ Audio Effects ▸ Noise Reduction/Restoration ▸ Voice Isolation; drop it on a clip like any audio effect. Amount (0–100 %, default 100 %) is how much of the cleaned voice you hear: lower values mix the original back in, keeping some room sound and hiding small artefacts. It can be keyframed.

q: How does DeepFilterNet tell speech from noise?
a: Classic noise reduction learns the noise floor and subtracts it, which only works while the noise stays the same. DeepFilterNet was trained on thousands of hours of speech and noise, so it recognises speech directly: it sets a gain for 32 frequency bands every 10 ms and, below 4.8 kHz, rebuilds the voice's fine detail from the last moments of sound. Revolution's port matches the original to within 16-bit precision.

q: Which commands manage the Voice Isolation model?
a: `audio.voiceIsolate.status`, `.download`, `.cancelDownload`, `.installFile` (with `path`, for offline computers) and `.remove`. The model is about 8 MB, MIT OR Apache-2.0, downloaded from the DeepFilterNet project's repository pinned to one release and checksum-checked.

q: What's the manual order for fixing a voice?
a: Listen first, on headphones, and fix only what you hear: 1. Reduce Rumble (about 3). 2. Noise: leave noise only heard in pauses, Reduce Noise at 3–5 for quiet steady noise, Voice Isolation at 7–10 for loud or changing noise. 3. DeHum at 50 or 60 Hz if there's a tone. 4. DeEss at 3–6. 5. Dynamics 2–3 for a steady speaker, 4–6 for one who moves. 6. EQ by taste. 7. Loudness last: Auto-Match to the target with Limit True Peak at −1 dBTP.

Dynamics 2–3 for a steady speaker, 4–6 for one who moves. 6. EQ by taste. 7. Loudness last: Auto-Match to the target with Limit True Peak at −1 dBTP.

q: and why loudness at the very end?
a: Because every step before it changes the level; matching loudness last means the delivered level is what you measured.

q: What does Clean Up Voice measure?
a: It measures the noise floor against the voice level, energy below 80 Hz, how sharp the s sounds are and how much the level varies; with the Voice Isolation model it also lets the model measure how much is noise (catching key clicks and wind gusts). It listens to the whole clip several times, in the background: a few seconds per minute of audio with the model.

q: How good is Clean Up Voice compared with doing it by hand?
a: On speech mixed with fan, room, traffic, keyboard and wind noise at several levels it came out as good as the manual process in every case (within 0.1 dB on traffic, keyboard and wind, ahead on fan and room) and closer to −14 LUFS, with the Voice Isolation model installed. Without the model, check by ear more carefully.

q: Where is the voice-over recording saved?
a: Voice-Over Record Settings (`audio.voiceover.settings`) set the microphone and input channel, the file name (default Voice-over), countdown beeps (on) and pre-roll / post-roll (2 s each). Recording is written as a mono WAV in the project's Scratch Disks folder (else next to the project), imported and placed on the track in one undo step; the pre-roll isn't kept.

q: What happens when I record over the same spot again?
a: Every recording is kept: recording again at the same point on the same track puts the new one on the timeline and keeps the earlier ones as takes. Select the clip and Essential Sound shows Takes; Use puts a take in place (full length from the record point) in one undo step, and the clip's processing (Clean Up Voice, Essential Sound settings, effects, clip gain) moves to it.

q: What standard does Auto-Match measure?
a: Auto-Match measures each selected clip's integrated loudness (EBU R128) and sets a match gain to its type's target: Dialogue −23, Music −25, SFX −21, Ambience −30 LUFS by default; preferences such as `audio.dialogueTargetLufs` change them. Limit True Peak holds peaks under a ceiling.

q: In Resolve I'd use Normalize Audio Levels. What's the equivalent?
a: Essential Sound ▸ Loudness ▸ Auto-Match (`essentialSound.autoMatch`) on the selected clips, with Limit True Peak for the ceiling. The mix's delivery level is a separate step (Clean Up Voice targets −14 LUFS for a voice).

q: In Resolve I'd set up sidechain ducking in Fairlight. How do I do that in Revolution?
a: On the Music or Ambience clip in Essential Sound turn Ducking on, choose what to duck against (e.g. Dialogue), set sensitivity, reduction and fades, then Generate Keyframes (`essentialSound.generateDucking`). It writes ordinary Volume keyframes you can move by hand.

q: What does Remix keep from the original song?
a: Remix rearranges only the middle: the intro still plays from the start and the song still ends on its real ending; the segment and variation sliders in Remix Properties choose between cut plans. Speed changes don't apply to a remixed clip, and Revert Remix brings it back as it was.

q: What's on a mixer strip?
a: Each audio track, submix and the master Mix has a strip: a fader (volume in dB), a pan knob, Mute, Solo, Record arm (for voice-over) and its automation mode. `mixer.setStrip` sets them (`volumeDb`, `pan`, `muted`, `solo`, `mode`, `output`); `mixer.inspect` lists every strip.

q: How do I set a track's fader from a script?
a: Each audio track, submix and the master Mix has a strip: a fader (volume in dB), a pan knob, Mute, Solo, Record arm (for voice-over) and its automation mode. `mixer.setStrip` sets them (`volumeDb`, `pan`, `muted`, `solo`, `mode`, `output`); `mixer.inspect` lists every strip.

q: How do I add an effect to a whole track?
a: `mixer.addInsert` puts an audio effect in a strip's slot (`effect`, `slot`, `postFader`), `mixer.setInsert` turns it on or off, moves it after the fader or sets parameters, `mixer.removeInsert` removes it. Clip effects fix one recording; track inserts give everything on a track the same treatment (even clips that don't need it), e.g. a limiter on the Mix.

q: Clip effect or track insert?
a: `mixer.addInsert` puts an audio effect in a strip's slot (`effect`, `slot`, `postFader`), `mixer.setInsert` turns it on or off, moves it after the fader or sets parameters, `mixer.removeInsert` removes it. Clip effects fix one recording; track inserts give everything on a track the same treatment (even clips that don't need it), e.g. a limiter on the Mix.

q: What is a submix?
a: A submix is a strip without clips that takes the sound of the tracks routed to it: add one with Add Audio Submix Track (`mixer.addSubmix`) and set tracks' output to it. A submix can feed a later submix, never an earlier one (no feedback loops). A send (`mixer.addSend`) sends a copy of a track at the send's level to a submix while the track stays on the Mix.

q: Can a submix feed another submix?

q: What does Read mode do?
a: Set the strip's automation mode, play and move its controls: you hear the moves at once and they're written as keyframes when playback stops (one undo step). Off ignores automation; Read (default) plays it; Latch records from the first touch and holds the last value; Touch records only while held and glides back; Write records every control from the start. Recorded moves are thinned into a few keyframes.

q: In Resolve I'd use Fairlight automation in Latch. How do I do that in Revolution?
a: Set the strip's automation mode to Latch in the Audio Track Mixer, play and move the fader: it records from the first touch and keeps the last value until playback stops. `mixer.recordStart` / `recordStop` drive it from a script.

q: How do I delete all keyframes in a track's volume lane?
a: `mixer.clearLane` removes a lane's keyframes; `mixer.setKeyframe` adds or changes one, `mixer.moveKeyframe` moves one, `mixer.deleteKeyframe` removes one. Lanes are `volume`, `pan`, `mute`, `send.<n>.level` and `fx.<slot>.<parameter>`.

q: What is the Audio Clip Mixer?
a: It looks like the track mixer, but its controls belong to the clip under the playhead on each track. With Off / Read / Latch / Touch / Write modes (`clipMixer.setMode`) a pass writes keyframes on the clips' own Volume and Panner effects, which travel with the clips; `clipMixer.set` sets one clip's level or pan directly.
